title: Enable skip_when_only for fmt and clippy checks in athena.toml
summary: Add skip_when_only = ["docs/", "*.md"] to the change capability's fmt and clippy checks in athena.toml. The test check keeps running on every change, because the xtask policy tests read docs/*.md and scan every tracked file, including .md files, for boundary terms. Update the CHANGELOG, which currently says enabling is a follow-up.

defaults_applied.how: One focused config change plus a changelog note.
The skip is enforced by the runner's skip_note logic, which already has tests.
The athena.toml comment says what the key does and why the test check is excluded.
The verifier runs test, clippy and fmt --check.

assumptions: The user's reply is read as: tests must not be skipped for files a test reads. I checked xtask/tests/policy.rs: it reads docs/non-rust-files.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/enforcement.md, and the boundary scan reads every tracked file outside records/, including all .md files. So no prose pattern is safe for the test check, and I leave it unskipped.
Clippy and fmt do not read prose, so skipping them on docs/ and *.md is safe. I did not check whether any crate uses include_str! on a .md file.
The pattern syntax is from path_matches in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs: 'dir/' matches a directory, '*.ext' matches any depth.

acceptance_criteria.text: In athena.toml, the [[capabilities.change.checks]] entries named fmt and clippy each have skip_when_only = ["docs/", "*.md"], and no other patterns.

The change capability's test check has no skip_when_only key, and athena.toml has a comment explaining why: xtask/tests/policy.rs reads docs/*.md and scans every tracked file, so a prose change can fail a test.
The [capabilities.study] checks and every other athena.toml key are unchanged.
CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased says the key is now enabled for fmt and clippy only, and the earlier 'does not set the key' follow-up wording no longer reads as pending.
Run `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`; all pass. The repository's config tests load athena.toml, so this shows it still parses.

out_of_scope: Changing the skip mechanism in Rust code
Skipping the test check for any path
departures: Slightly higher pass probability and lower cost than the reference, because the change is a small config edit plus a changelog line.
